name: W31 Morning Flow — Thoracic Week: Thread-the-Needle and Puppy Pose Return
description:
The daily 15-minute opener. **The stretches point at the upper back this week, on purpose.** A new crackle showed up in the left shoulder on the pull-up bar, and several weeks of sleeping on a couch is a better explanation for it than anything in the program — so thread-the-needle and puppy pose come back after months away, both of them upper-back and shoulder openers.

**The work block rotates to dead bug and glute bridge**, with the side plank staying because one-armed baby carrying never rotates out.

**Cat-cow and the low-lunge rotation open** instead of the inchworm work. Anchors hold: scorpion, lizard, cossack, pigeon, and the push-up greasing set.

Use the tired-day version whenever the night was bad. Doing it badly beats skipping it.

sets.name: ☀️ Through the Day — Small and Often (Not Now)
sets.notes: Not part of the morning sequence — these are the reminders that get sprinkled through the day.

exercises.notes: Once an hour if you can. Heels down, easy breathing, a little deeper each time.
30s each foot. Let the **ankle** do the correcting, not the hip. Fingertip on a wall is fine on no sleep.
Heel glued down, knee over the toes. **Still no measurement** — the baseline is banked (right 1.5 fists, left 1 fist) and the re-measure is a few weeks out. Just do the reps.
Sole turns **outward** against the band, shin still. The left one is the point.

sets.name: Primer — Spine First (~3 min)
sets.notes: Keep moving between shapes rather than settling into holds. The long holds come at the end, when you are warm.

exercises.notes: **Back after a long absence, and it leads this week for a reason.** Move one vertebra at a time rather than hinging at the middle — the upper back is the part that has been locked into a couch all night.
30s each side. Deep lunge, hand down, **rotate the top arm to the ceiling and follow it with your eyes.** Hips and upper back in one shape.
Tight fists, thumbs tucked, hinged slightly forward. **This is the brace the squat is asking for** — wake it here so it is available later.

sets.name: Work Block — Anti-Extension, Glutes, Anti-Side-Bend (~5 min)
sets.notes: Activate, do not fatigue. **Same three jobs as last week's Big 3, different three moves** — one resists the back arching, one wakes the glutes, one resists side-bending. The side plank stays because carrying a baby on one hip never rotates out.

exercises.notes: **The greasing set — one quick set, never to failure.** Elbows ~45°, **pack down not up.** A daily habit, not a training stimulus.
Opposite arm and leg reach away slowly. **The low back stays pressed flat the entire time** — the moment it lifts off the floor, that rep was the last one. Slow beats far.
Drive through the heels, **squeeze the glutes at the top and hold a beat.** Ribs down — if the low back is doing the lifting, the glutes are asleep and this is the wake-up call before the hinge work.
**Anti-lateral-flexion, the direct counter to carrying a baby on one hip.** 30s each side. Stack shoulders and hips, drive the bottom hip up, neck long. Drop to the knee if the shape breaks.

sets.name: Barre Leg Block — Plié Work (~4 min)
sets.notes:
**Action Jacqueline-style leg work, added because the flow was running short.** All three are bodyweight or mat — no barre needed, a counter or chair back is plenty if you want a hand.

**⚠️ On legs day, halve this or skip it.** The work block is supposed to activate, not fatigue, and these pulses genuinely tire the quads and inner thighs. Before push or pull it is free; before squats it is not.

exercises.notes:
**Feet wide, toes turned out.** Sink into a wide plié — thighs toward parallel — and pulse small and low.
- **Knees track out over the toes**, never caving in
- Ribs down, tailbone heavy, chest tall
- The burn is the inner thigh and it arrives fast — that is the move working, not a problem

**Plié, then rise onto the toes, then straighten.** One continuous shape change rather than three poses.
- **Rise from the plié without letting the knees fall in**
- A fingertip on a counter is fine — it is an ankle and calf drill as much as a leg one, and your left ankle is the one worth watching

**On all fours, lift one bent knee out to the side.**
- **Hips stay square to the floor** — the moment the torso rolls away to get height, the range is too big
- Slow up, slower down
- Same side-of-the-hip target as the abduction machine, which is useful the week that machine is unreliable

sets.name: Yoga Flow — Thoracic + Hip Arc (~7 min)
sets.notes: Goes last because warm muscle stretches deeper. One continuous arc, not a list of holds. **Two of these are aimed at the upper back and shoulders this week** — take your time in them.

exercises.notes: 30s each side. Thoracic rotation and hip flexor in one shape.
45s each side. Deep lunge, both hands inside the front foot. Forearms if the hip allows.
**Your readiness screen.** Slow, deep, heel down. Read it as a delta against your own normal — the old ankle sprain means a stiff day here is not a bad-session forecast.

**Back after months, and it is this week's most useful minute.** From all fours, slide one arm under the other and let the shoulder and side of the head rest down. **Keep the hips stacked over the knees** — if they drift, the rotation leaks into the low back. Breathe into the space between the shoulder blades.

**Also back after months.** Hips stay high over the knees, hands walk forward, chest melts toward the floor. **This is the undo for a night on a couch** — the upper back extends and both shoulders open overhead at once. Go slow if the left one talks.
45s each side. Finish here. Let the hips settle before the day starts.

sets.name: 📍 Day-Specific Add-On — Pick by Today's Training (~3-5 min)
sets.notes: Pick only the block that matches today. Two or three moves, not the whole list.

exercises.notes: **Push day.** 30s each arm, elbow at MID height.
**Push day. Rehab anchor.** Thumbs up, lift from the mid-back — the neck stays out of it.
**Push day. Rehab anchor.** Arms stay straight; only the blades move.
**Pull day. Rehab anchor.** Easy decompression before loaded pulling.
**Pull day. Rehab anchor.** Pack down first — the elbows do not bend. **Both shoulders were crackly last week, so take these slower than usual and notice which side is noisier.**

**Pull day — it worked, so it stays.** One light set before the pull-up bar, then **hold a light DB still at about 90° for 30 seconds.** A still, moderate load is the calmest thing you can give an irritable tendon, and it goes in before anything hangs off the elbow.
**Pull or KB day. Rehab anchor.** Elbow pinned to the ribs, light or no weight.
**KB day. Rehab anchor.** Ribs down; only the range that stays smooth.
**Legs day.** Toe to wall, heel glued down. No measurement — just the reps, before the heels go up on the plates.
**Legs day.** 30s each side for the lateral chain.

tips: Thread-the-needle and puppy pose are the two that matter this week — the left shoulder and the couch are the reason.
Dead bug: the low back stays flat. Slow beats far.
Cossack squat is the readiness screen, not a stretch to push.
Tired-day version: half the reps, half the hold times. Doing it badly beats skipping it.
Pick only the day-specific add-on that matches today's training.
